The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 147 from H Masakadza, complemented by a commanding 142-run stand between PJ Moor and H Masakadza that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.97 RPO. West Indies's bowling response was spearheaded by KAJ Roach (3/43), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Concluding at 326/10 (109.1 ov), Zimbabwe posted a competitive total, ensuring a closely matched contest.

The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 110 from JO Holder, complemented by a commanding 212-run stand between JO Holder and SO Dowrich that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.51 RPO. Zimbabwe's bowling response was spearheaded by Sikandar Raza (5/99), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Reaching 448/10 (178.2 ov), West Indies's innings completed the first-innings exchange (122 Runs (West Indies)), shaping the strategic contours for the second half of the Test.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: Entering the third innings with the match balance in flux, Zimbabwe sought to extend their lead and set a decisive fourth-innings target. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 89 from Sikandar Raza, complemented by a commanding 98-run stand between Sikandar Raza and PJ Moor that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.09 RPO. ST Gabriel (2/33) maintained tight lines for West Indies, creating intermittent chances in an otherwise demanding fielding effort. Zimbabwe's total of 301/7 (143.6 ov) closed their second innings, cementing a formidable target and transferring immense pressure onto the opposition.

summaryTab.matchStory: Zimbabwe recovered from early pressure in the first innings, anchored by H Masakadza's resolute 147 to post 326. West Indies replied strongly with 448, powered by JO Holder's commanding century (110) to swing the contest. Zimbabwe posted 301/7 in their second innings, shifting match momentum decisively through crucial partnerships. A resilient final-day rearguard ensured the match concluded in a fiercely contested draw.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Queens Sports Club commenced with high tactical intensity as Zimbabwe posted 326/10 (109.1 ov) in their opening innings. In response, West Indies countered with 448/10 (178.2 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 212-Run Stand: JO Holder & SO Dowrich, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Sikandar Raza delivered a masterclass for Zimbabwe (169 Runs & 5 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Match Drawn 52%) and allowing Match Drawn to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, West Indies faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Match Drawn's bowling unit, bolstered by H Masakadza (152 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Match drawn in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Match Drawn's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While West Indies produced fighting phases, Match Drawn won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
